references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews directly quotes this text about a 'root of bitterness' that grows up and causes trouble, warning against anyone falling away from God's grace.
The same context about turning away from the Lord to serve other gods, with warnings against deception within the family or tribe.
Warns against the heart turning away and worshiping other gods, addressing the same theme of apostasy.
Concerns a man or woman who does evil by serving other gods, using similar wording and themes.
Peter tells Simon that he is in 'the gall of bitterness,' reflecting the image of a bitter root and poison.
Refers to walking according to one's own stubborn heart and following Baal, and that God gives them wormwood to eat.
God gives false prophets wormwood to eat and poison to drink, using the same imagery of wormwood.
Amos uses the image of turning justice into wormwood, a similar use of wormwood as a symbol of bitterness.
Hosea describes judgment growing up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the field, a similar image of toxic growth.
